sources.names.given: Opened 2026-10-17: beliebte-vornamen.de decade pages (e.g. https://www.beliebte-vornamen.de/jahr/1970er, 1930er to 2020er), Knud Bielefeld, 'eigene Recherchen anhand einer repraesentativen Stichprobe' (Germany-wide, not Niedersachsen; site copyright is the compiler's, only the rank order is used here as a frequency, no text copied). Cohort = the decade of birth (1930 to 2020), top 35 of each sex (30 for the 2010s), weight = round(6000/(rank+6)): ranks turned into counts, an assumed Zipf-like decay (PLACEHOLDER shape, to confirm against counts). Figures were read through a page summariser, so rank order may drift slightly. Names are drawn at random from frequencies only; a drawn name may coincide with a living person by chance. sources.decisions.benefit_decision.pension: An objection (Widerspruch) within one month of the notice (Sozialgerichtsgesetz s 84: recalled, to confirm), required before a claim to the social court (s 78), which is brought within one month of the decision on the objection (s 87: recalled, to confirm) and is free of court fees for recipients (s 183: recalled, to confirm). An objection not decided within three months may be taken to the social court as an action for failure to act (Untaetigkeitsklage, Sozialgerichtsgesetz s 88(2): recalled, to confirm); modelled as a deemed refusal after 91 days, from which the month to go to court runs (the real action has no such month: ours is the stricter reading). The claimant must supply what the authority asks for within a reasonable time it sets (SGB I s 60: recalled, to confirm); 14 days is a PLACEHOLDER.
sources.decisions.benefit_decision.unemployment-: As the pension. The employer must issue the employment certificate (Arbeitsbescheinigung) on the end of a job (SGB III s 312: recalled, to confirm); its 14 days is a PLACEHOLDER, and the claim is decided without it if it does not come.
sources.decisions.benefit_decision.unemployment: As the pension (Sozialgerichtsgesetz s 84, 78, 87, 88(2), 183: recalled, to confirm; the deemed refusal after 91 days likewise); 14 days for the documents asked for is a PLACEHOLDER.
sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.
sources.culture.origin: PLACE: Lower Saxony (Niedersachsen), Mikrozensus 2024 first results, migration background as the statistics office defines it (a person or at least one parent not born with German nationality). groups: LSN, 'Integrationsreport Niedersachsen 2025', https://www.stk.niedersachsen.de/download/224449/Integrationsreport_Niedersachsen_2025.pdf , OPENED 2026-10-13: population 7,921,000; without migration background 5,863,000 (74.0%); with 2,058,000 (26.0%). The split of the 26.0% is (to confirm), built from two sources of different bases: foreigners in Lower Saxony 1,093,110 at 2024-12-31 (Ausländerzentralregister, same report, OPENED) taken as 13.8% of 7,921,000, the rest of those with a migration background (12.2%) with German nationality. The statistics' split into immigrants and those born in Germany was not found. same_household_bps: 6758 PLACEHOLDER, DERIVED, not a statistic: no table of couples by migration background for Lower Saxony was found and opened. It is the chance share of same-group couples from these three groups (sum of squares, 58.2%) raised by the homophily below as c(1+h)/(c(1+h)+1-c) with h=0.5. homophily_bps: PLACEHOLDER 5000 (a close tie is half again as likely within a group as by chance). No survey of close ties or friendship by group for this place was found and opened; McPherson, Smith-Lovin and Cook 2001 ('Birds of a feather', Annual Review of Sociology 27) gives the general fact, not this place's figure. CHILDREN: the definition counts a child with migration background if either parent was not born with German nationality, so a child of a mixed couple is counted in a migration-background group (the either-parent rule is of the right kind), but the statistics do not say which of the two migration groups (nationality) the child is put in.
sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: Statistische Aemter des Bundes und der Laender, Mikrozensus 2022, Zusatzprogramm Wohnen, Standardtabelle WO 08 (main-tenant households by rent burden), sheet Niedersachsen (https://www.statistikportal.de/sites/default/files/2025-05/wo08_mz2022.xlsx, opened 2026-10-12): of 1,523 thousand main-tenant households, 59 under 10%, 448 at 10 to 20, 482 at 20 to 30, 270 at 30 to 40, 136 at 40 to 50, 115 at 50% or more (13 thousand not allocated, left out). Gross cold rent over the household's NET monthly income, so wages are counted here after what is withheld. Mean 28.1% (26.3% in small towns and rural municipalities; WO 05). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.
sources.support.take_up_bps: pension 89.7%: recipients of a statutory old-age pension over the population aged 65 and over (a search summary in the style of the Deutsche Rentenversicherung's Rentenatlas; not opened, and the base is 65 and over where the pension here starts at 67: to confirm). unemployment 60%: of 3.061 million unemployed in August 2026, 1.838 million (60%) were in the basic-income system (SGB II) and 40% in unemployment insurance (Bundesagentur fuer Arbeit, Monatsbericht zum Arbeits- und Ausbildungsmarkt, August 2026, section 1.4.3, https://statistik.arbeitsagentur.de/Statistikdaten/Detail/202608/arbeitsmarktberichte/monatsbericht-monatsbericht/monatsbericht-d-0-202608-pdf.pdf, opened 2026-10-12). Only the basic income (`unemployment`) can open in payment: the insurance payment is reckoned from a record of contributions nobody has on the first day. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Payments in force"): of those the payment's rule already entitles as the year begins, this share open with it in payment; the rest claim it when they first look, as before.
sources.ownership.owner_bps_by_age: Destatis and the statistical offices of the Laender, Wohnen in Deutschland, Mikrozensus Zusatzprogramm Wohnen 2022, Tabelle 1 (https://www.statistikportal.de/sites/default/files/2025-05/Wohnen_in_Deutschland_2022.xlsx, opened 2026-10-12): households in owner-occupied dwellings by age of the main income earner, Germany: 8.1% under 25, 26.4% at 25-44, 50.4% at 45-64, 51.2% at 65 and over (41.9% overall; Niedersachsen 49.0% overall, no split by age found). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): only as how much likelier a household of one age is than another to be among the town's owners; their number is the houses the profile's house_owner_bps makes owner-occupied.
sources.households.kin_households_most_bps: 1%, TO CONFIRM: households of three or more generations were 'under 1%' in 2022 (Destatis, press release N037 of 22 June 2023, https://www.destatis.de/DE/Presse/Pressemitteilungen/2023/06/PD23_N037_12_63.html, opened 2026-10-12; national, and the release does not make clear whether the base is all households or those of more than one person). The ceiling is set at that bound. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/households.md, "Taken in"): a ceiling and nothing else: no more households than this hold kin when people with nothing coming in are placed with a household that can carry them.
sources.tenancy.possession: Buergerliches Gesetzbuch ss 543(2) no. 3 and 569: a landlord may end the tenancy without notice once two months' rent is owed, and a tenant who pays everything within two months of being served with the action for eviction cures it (the Schonfristzahlung: plan_months 2 stands for it); eviction is by the Gerichtsvollzieher, who gives some three weeks' notice (to confirm: recalled, the Code not opened). notice_days 14 and possession_days 30 are PLACEHOLDERS. The police stand for the Gerichtsvollzieher. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for this place of how many tenants served with an application for possession answer it in writing or attend; it is the middle of the two figures opened for other places: 43% of hearings with the renter or someone for them in Victoria, 39.3% of tenants present in Cleveland, Ohio). plan_consider 'none', plan_months 0 (it was 2, which stood for the same rule) and cure_days 60: the court sets no plan; the ending of the tenancy has no effect if the landlord is paid everything owed within two months of the claim being served (BGB s 569(3) no. 2, opened 2026-10-12; not where it was already used in the two years before, which is left out). 2026-10-16: BGB para 543(2) no. 3 (two months' rent owed), para 543(3) (no prior warning needed for arrears) and para 569(3) no. 2 (a notice is void if the landlord is paid, or a public body commits to pay, within two months of the action becoming pending) were opened (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__543.html and __569.html) and agree with arrears_days 60 and cure_days 60. eviction_notice_days, notice_days, possession_days and stay_past_notice_bps: not found (ZPO para 885a not opened).
sources.business.entry_bps_per_year: Enterprise birth rate, Germany, births over active enterprises, business economy except public administration and membership organisations: 7.81% (2021), 7.98% (2022), 8.43% (2023), 7.78% (2024); births 245,746, 252,479, 268,936 and 252,090 (Eurostat, business demography, table bd_size, indicator ENT_BRTHR_PC, API https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/bd_size, opened 2026-10-16). 778 is the 2024 value; the average of 2021 to 2024 is 800. National, not Lower Saxony; it counts businesses with no employees. Replaces the PLACEHOLDER 870 (8 to 9%, recalled). HOW IT IS USED: a target a town's business births are compared with (docs/calibration.md); nothing sets births, which follow expected profit (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "Entry by expected profit").
sources.employment.hours: Sozialgesetzbuch III ss 95-105 (Kurzarbeit; opened at gesetze-im-internet.de, ss 96, 99, 104, 105): an employer needs a legal basis to cut hours (a contract clause, a collective or works agreement, or the employee's agreement), reports the stoppage to the employment agency, and Kurzarbeitergeld of 60% (67% with a child) of the loss of net pay is paid for up to 12 months by the agency, not the employer (ss 104, 105). Here: with the employee's agreement, any hours, 365 days a spell. NOT BUILT: the agency's payment to the worker, so a worker on cut hours here loses more than a real one; the 40-hour ordinary week is a placeholder (full-time contracts run 35 to 40; the Arbeitszeitgesetz caps at 48). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first.
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Buergerliches Gesetzbuch s 622 (notice: four weeks, rising with service to seven months at twenty years); Kuendigungsschutzgesetz s 1a (half a month's pay for each year of service where the employer offers it on a dismissal for operational reasons: taken as paid, which overstates it, since it is an option and many dismissals are settled otherwise) and s 23 (the Act does not bind establishments of ten or fewer). Short-time work (Kurzarbeit) is not modelled (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it.
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (14.7% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (6.5%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (13.5%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (15.4%). goods: a consumer problem (31.3%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). 2026-10-16 (no change): wages 325 lies inside the sourced range for the share of employees paid under the statutory minimum wage (2 to 4% in the earnings surveys, 5 to 12% in the SOEP, 6.6% in 2023; Goerke and Pannenberg, WSI-Mitteilungen 2/2026, https://www.wsi.de/data/wsimit_2026_02_goerke-1.pdf, and DIW Wochenbericht 28/2019: 7.7% of those entitled in 2017, opened); a stock of low hourly pay at a point in time, not a yearly incidence of trouble getting wages agreed. pay_short_by_bps, bill_over_bps, goods_faulty_share_bps, repair_hours: searched (the energy ombudsman's report was not reachable), no figure found. put_right_on_asking_bps: the energy ombudsman says about 80% of procedures end in agreement (a managing director's interview, search summary), the telecoms ombudsman 47% (Bundesnetzagentur, Schlichtung TK 2024, opened); cases that failed bilateral resolution first, so not comparable with 42.9%.
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. PLACEHOLDERS, every one: each stands at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (42.9%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.

sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time, a placeholder fortnight, and a daily capacity; both are gone: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. A town now opens with the payments its people are already entitled to in force (granted before the year, never decided in it), so it decides fewer claims and refuses fewer (Victoria 37.8 to 24.8 a year). It is NOT re-fitted: that would be fitting an outcome again. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force'). 2026-10-16 (NOT applied: a different quantity): objections (Widersprueche) in SGB II in 2025: 476,728 decided and 147,213 upheld in whole or part, 30.9%; objections were 2.1% of decisions in the joint jobcentres; of lawsuits (52,858 decided) just under a third led to a new decision (Bundesagentur fuer Arbeit, press release March 2026, https://www.arbeitsagentur.de/presse/2026-03-buergergeld; Bundestag Drucksache 21/3177, opened). Decisions overturned on objection are about 0.65% of all decisions, about 1.0% with lawsuits: a share of decisions of every kind (amounts, stops, repayment demands), not of qualifying claims wrongly refused, and a lower bound (many errors are never appealed). 898 stays the fitted stand-in.

sources.frictions.venues: tribunal_days 164: the average duration of proceedings to disposal at the Amtsgerichte in civil matters in Niedersachsen, 5.4 months in 2025 (and in 2024; the federal figure was 5.3 in 2024), at 30.4 days a month = 164 days (Niedersaechsisches Justizministerium, 'Justiz in Niedersachsen: Zahlen, Daten, Fakten', https://justizportal.niedersachsen.de/download/128838/Justiz_in_Niedersachsen_-_Zahlen_Daten_Fakten_-_Flyer_PDF_ist_nicht_barrierefrei_.pdf, the table of the duration of proceedings, opened 2026-10-16). The Amtsgericht is the town's tribunal for tenancy, goods and small claims; the Arbeitsgerichte, which hear wages, take 2.9 months (3.1 in 2025), about 90 days (same flyer; Landesarbeitsgericht Niedersachsen, Jahresbericht 2024, https://landesarbeitsgericht.niedersachsen.de/download/217771, opened). The profile has one number for both tribunals, so the civil figure is taken. It is an average over all cases that ended (withdrawals and settlements too), not the time to a first hearing, so it overstates the time to a hearing. Replaces the placeholder six weeks (42 days). tribunal_fee_hours_of_pay 9.6: the court fee for a first-instance civil case is 3.0 fee units (GKG Anlage 1, Nr. 1210; 1.0 on withdrawal or settlement, Nr. 1211); a unit is EUR 40.00 up to a claim of EUR 500, EUR 61.00 up to EUR 1,000 and EUR 170.50 up to EUR 5,000 (GKG Anlage 2 as amended by BGBl. 2025 I Nr. 109), paid in advance (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/gkg_2004/anlage_1.html and anlage_2.html, opened through a fetch summary 2026-10-16: amounts as the summary gave them). For a claim of EUR 1,000 the fee is EUR 183; over the profile's shop pay (148,431 cents over 78 hours a fortnight = EUR 19.03 an hour) that is 9.6 hours; a claim of EUR 500 is 6.3 hours and one of EUR 5,000 is 26.9. The labour court's fees (GKG Part 8: none for the conciliation, a fee on judgment) were not opened, and there a worker pays less. Replaces the placeholder 3. answer_days 14 (the labour court sets the conciliation hearing within two weeks, ArbGG para 61a(2), already cited; that is a time to a hearing, not the other side's time to answer): kept. uphold_without_proof_bps: PLACEHOLDER, no figure was found.
sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for Germany, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency).
sources.outlook.residence: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for how long people have lived at their address was found for Germany on a page opened. Borrowed from Australia's (the only place whose figures were opened), for lack of any: ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator. Germany's own are probably different (to source: Census or housing-survey tables of years since moving in).
sources.outlook.job_tenure: How long employed people have been with their current employer (starting attachment to the trade). OECD, 'Employment by job tenure intervals' (dataset OECD.ELS.SAE DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ, measure TENURE_EMP, share of employment by time with the current employer; both sexes, all ages), national figures for Germany, 2025 for under 1 year and 10 and over, and 2024 for the three bands between (the 2025 release gives 1 to under 10 years only as one band), so the bands mix two years; read from the OECD SDMX API (sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ) on 2026-10-11, the response opened and the figures copied: under 1 year, 1 to under 3, 3 to under 5, 5 to under 10, 10 and over. National, not the region's: none by region was found. It covers the employed (employees and the self-employed), where a person's tenure is the time in the present job. The open band (10 and over) is read as 10 to 30 years by the generator. The shares sum to 99.9 to 100 in the source and are scaled to 10000.
sources.currency: Euro, in cents: ISO 4217 EUR, two decimal places. Written with the euro sign, or in words as euros and cents. How its people write money: a comma before the decimals, points between thousands, the sign after the digits with a space ("1.234,56 €"). Unicode CLDR (cldr-json, cldr-numbers-full/main/de/numbers.json, opened 2026-10-08): decimal ',', group '.', currency pattern '#,##0.00 ¤' (CLDR's space there is a no-break space; a plain one is written here and either is read). DIN 5008 and the Duden were not opened (a web search summary only).
sources.health: The clinic stands for the town's health system (general practice and the hospital it refers to; a liberty). doctor_wage_per_pay_period: EUR 8,634 a month, the median gross monthly pay (without special payments) of full-time doctors (KldB 814, Human- und Zahnmedizin), April 2025, times 12 over 26 (Destatis, table 62361-03, as under wages_per_pay_period, opened); national, not the clinic's own agreement. doctors_per_1000: placeholder, about 0.7 full-time-equivalent general practitioners per 1,000 people, recalled from a count of about 5,000-5,500 Hausaerzte in Niedersachsen (Kassenaerztliche Vereinigung Niedersachsen); the Bundesaerztekammer and KVN statistics pages could not be opened (404), so not confirmed. consult_minutes, seek_care_bps, treats and off_work_severities: placeholders as in the Australian profile (conditions here are hospital-level; care shortens them by a fifth; nobody works with a serious or severe condition). Statutory health insurance covers nearly everyone; nothing is charged at the clinic here (a liberty). 2026-10-16: doctors_per_1000 0.63 (was the placeholder 0.7): 5,048 general practitioners (Hausaerzte) in the area of the Kassenaerztliche Vereinigung Niedersachsen in 2024, counted by Anrechnungsfaktor, the planning weight by working time and so close to full-time equivalents (KVN, 'Arztzahlprognose 2040', https://www.kvn.de/media/Mitglieder/Publikationen/Arztzahlprognose+2040.pdf, opened 2026-10-16), over about 8.0 million residents (7,921,000 in the Mikrozensus 2024). Contract (Kassen) doctors only.
sources.round: Working hours 8 to 16, Monday to Friday, for everyone, shops included (a liberty: German shops open Saturdays and, by Land law, close on Sundays; Niedersachsen's Ladenoeffnungsgesetz allows Monday to Saturday; to confirm); average usual weekly hours of full-time employees are 39.1 (Destatis, Durchschnittliche Bruttoverdienste und Arbeitszeiten, April 2025, https://www.destatis.de/DE/Themen/Arbeit/Verdienste/Verdienste-Branche-Berufe/Tabellen/bruttomonats-verdienste-stichmonat.html), so 8 hours a day with the lunch break outside it. School 8 to 13 on school days (primary and secondary schools in Niedersachsen mostly end around 13:00 without all-day provision; placeholder, to confirm). Travel: off the roads a 25 m cell on foot in about 18 seconds (walking about 1.4 m/s: Bohannon 1997; to confirm); on a road about 2 seconds (50 km/h, the general urban limit in the Strassenverkehrs-Ordnung, StVO para 3(3); to confirm); slower across water, wetland and bush (placeholders). Roads budget about EUR 300 a resident a year: placeholder carried over from the Australian profile; no German municipal road-spending figure was found.
sources.ownership: house_owner_bps: placeholder, 80% of separate houses owner-occupied. LSN reports that 47.7% of dwellings in Niedersachsen are owner-occupied and 47.0% rented (Zensus 2022, https://www.statistik.niedersachsen.de/zensus2022/ergebnisse-des-zensus-2022-233166.html, opened) and that about half of all households own their home (press release 074/2025); owner-occupation is much higher in houses than in flats, but the Zensus table by building type was not opened (to confirm); flats here are all rented (a liberty). mortgage_bps_by_age: placeholder carried over (most owners under 45 have a mortgage, few over 65; Bundesbank PHF would give it, to source). mortgage_payment_per_month: derived, not observed: 80% of the median asking price of a one- or two-family house (EUR 339,000, empirica for LBS NordWest, 2025: see public_finance.median_house_price) over 30 years at 3.8% is about EUR 1,264 a month. mortgage_rate_bps: placeholder 3.8%, a guess for 10-year-fixed home loans with the ECB deposit rate at 2.5% (Bundesbank MFI interest rate statistics, new housing loans; to source). mortgage_years_left: placeholder. market: deposit 20% (lenders expect about 20% equity; placeholder, to confirm); costs 10.5%: land transfer tax in Niedersachsen 5.0% (Niedersaechsisches Grunderwerbsteuergesetz; to confirm), notary and land register about 2%, and the buyer's half of a typical 7.14% estate agent's commission, 3.57% (to confirm); a 30-year term (placeholder; German loans fix the rate for 10-15 years); buy_bps_per_month, relist_days, cut_bps and floor_bps: placeholders as in the Australian profile (Merlo and Ortalo-Magne 2004; to confirm).
sources.utilities: Water: 126 litres a person a day for households in Germany (Destatis, Wasserwirtschaft page, opened 2026-10-08). Price: EUR 1.82 a cubic metre for drinking water in Niedersachsen on 1 January 2025 plus a household-usual basic charge of EUR 93.15 a year (EUR 23.29 a quarter), population-weighted over tariff areas (Destatis, table 'Entgelt fuer die Trinkwasserversorgung in Tarifgebieten nach Tariftypen 2023 bis 2025', Land Niedersachsen, 'Kubikmeter- und Grundentgelt', https://www.destatis.de/DE/Themen/Gesellschaft-Umwelt/Umwelt/Wasserwirtschaft/Tabellen/tw-09-entgelt-trinkwasserversorgung-tarifgeb-nach-tariftypen-2023-2025-land-bund.html, opened), plus waste water at the national EUR 2.62-2.71 a cubic metre in 2025 (take 2.65; same Destatis series, table aw-07, Germany only, opened), so EUR 4.47 a kilolitre. Bills go to owners. River inflow, flow and losses are placeholders sized so a small town's draw is a small share of a modest river. Energy: price_per_kwh 37 cents, the average household electricity price in 2026 at 3,500 kWh a year with the base charge included (BDEW Strompreisanalyse August 2026, https://www.bdew.de/service/daten-und-grafiken/bdew-strompreisanalyse/, opened); because the base charge is already in it, supply_per_day is 0. grid_price_per_kwh: 24 cents, procurement and sales (15.2 ct) plus network charges (9.2 ct) of that price, the rest (12.6 ct) being taxes, levies and surcharges (same page, opened); here the town's retailer keeps the 12.6 ct (see gaps). kwh_per_household_per_day: 7, placeholder (about 2,500 kWh a year for an average household of two people; not opened). grid_emissions_g_per_kwh: 344 g CO2 per kWh of electricity consumed in Germany in 2025 (Umweltbundesamt, Strom- und Waermeversorgung in Zahlen, https://www.umweltbundesamt.de/themen/klima-energie/energieversorgung/strom-waermeversorgung-in-zahlen, opened).
sources.climate: Weather drawn for each run (docs/behaviour/weather.md). Opened: Deutscher Wetterdienst climate normals 1991-2020 (https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/observations_germany/climate/multi_annual/mean_91-20/): Hannover station (id 2014) has 7.7 hot days (30 C or more) a year, 7.3 of them in June to August, and 36 summer days (25 C or more); Celle station (id 850) has 680 mm of precipitation a year, from 40 mm (April) to 74 mm (July). heatwave_bps_per_week is derived: 7.7 hot days over spells of about 4 days is about 1.9 spells in the 13 weeks of June to August, 1,480 basis points a week (rounded from the formula; not every hot day starts a spell of 3-5 days, so it is an upper reading). rain_by_month_bps: the river's flow by month is not precipitation (northern German rivers peak in winter and early spring because evaporation is low; lowest in late summer and early autumn; BfG / NLWKN gauge data were not fetched), so the monthly shape is a placeholder (10,000 = the year's mean). storm_*: heavy-rain spells, placeholder (the floods of December 2023 to January 2024 in Niedersachsen show the order of rarity; NLWKN reports not opened). drought_*: placeholder (Germany had droughts in 2018-2020 and 2022). Heatwave length, heat units and the illness gradient are carried over from the Australian profile (Robert Koch Institute heat-death estimates not opened). warning_lead_days: placeholder.
sources.hazards: Floods: placeholders sized against the river as modelled, as in the Australian profile (about 9,000 kL a 25 m cell in the usual flow; it spills past 12,000, 30% of the excess a day; a building floods above 300 kL on its cell; wetland soaks up 500 kL a cell a day). Real record to calibrate against: the December 2023 to January 2024 flood in Niedersachsen (NLWKN, Hochwasser Dezember 2023 / Januar 2024; to confirm). Emergency relief is run by Landkreis and Gemeinde fire services and the Technisches Hilfswerk (Niedersaechsisches Katastrophenschutzgesetz; to confirm): here the town hall.
sources.crime: Crime, deliberately rare and driven by circumstance only (Becker 1968; Cohen and Felson 1979), never by any group. take_bps_per_month_in_need, caught_bps_reckoned, take_quantity, investigation_hours: placeholders. detection_bps: placeholder 30%, recalled from the national figure that about three theft offences in ten are cleared (Bundeskriminalamt, Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik, Diebstahl insgesamt; to confirm; Niedersachsen's overall clearance rate for all offences was 62.72% in 2025 and it recorded 156,725 thefts, Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik Niedersachsen 2025, https://www.mi.niedersachsen.de/download/226742/Handout_Polizeiliche_Kriminalstatistik_2025_Niedersachsen.pdf; the theft clearance rate itself was in a chart that could not be read). police_per_1000: placeholder 2.4 sworn officers per 1,000, recalled order of magnitude for the Landespolizei Niedersachsen (to confirm). officer_wage_per_pay_period: placeholder EUR 4,000 a month for a Polizeikommissar (grade A9, Niedersaechsische Besoldungstabelle; to confirm), times 12 over 26. 2026-10-16 (not applied): police_per_1000 2.4: Landespolizei Niedersachsen 23,435 persons (head count, 30 June 2024, including police administration staff) over 7.9 to 8.0 million residents = 2.96; at the Land's FTE-to-head-count ratio of 0.86 about 2.5 (Personalstrukturbericht 2024, https://www.mi.niedersachsen.de/download/228411/Personalstrukurbericht_2024.pdf, sections 2.2.1, opened): the sworn FTE count was not read, so 2.4 stands. detection_bps 3000: Niedersachsen's clearance of theft is about 36% (Polizeiliche Kriminalstatistik 2025, https://www.mi.niedersachsen.de/download/226742/Handout_Polizeiliche_Kriminalstatistik_2025_Niedersachsen.pdf, opened; which of two labels, 35.86% and 36.30%, is which year is uncertain), but a case cleared by naming a suspect is not detection: not applied.
sources.justice: The tribunal stands for the civil and labour courts (Amtsgericht for tenancy and small claims; Arbeitsgericht for unpaid wages). hearing_after_days: 14, since 'the conciliation hearing (Guteverhandlung) is to be held within two weeks of the filing of the claim' (Arbeitsgerichtsgesetz para 61a(2), https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/arbgg/__61a.html, opened); civil courts take longer (months). pay_within_days, challenge_bps, apply_bps, apply_after_days: placeholders carried over from the Australian profile; no German figure found (Destatis Rechtspflege tables were not reached). A money judgment is enforced by an attachment of the debtor's bank account (Kontopfaendung, ZPO para 829 ff.; not opened).
sources.education: school_ages: schooling is compulsory from the school year in which a child turns 6 (cut-off 30 September) for 12 years, 9 in full-time schooling and the rest part-time (Niedersaechsisches Schulgesetz para 63-66; to confirm); 6 to 17 here. students_per_teacher: placeholder 15 for general schools (Destatis' 2025/26 report on general schools, opened, gives Niedersachsen's 72,952 teachers by head count, not full-time equivalents, and national pupils of about 9.0 million, so no clean ratio; recalled about 15, to confirm). school_days_per_year: about 190, derived: 261 weekdays less about 12 weeks of school holidays and public holidays in term (Niedersachsen's holiday calendar; to confirm). hours_per_day: 5 (8:00 to 13:00; placeholder). teacher_wage_per_pay_period: placeholder, EUR 5,200 a month gross for a teacher in grade A12/A13 (Niedersaechsische Besoldungstabelle; to confirm), times 12 over 26. attainment: placeholder shapes from OECD (tried: Destatis' 'Bevoelkerung nach Bildungsabschluss' table, opened, gives 2019 shares of all people aged 15 and over, 25.2% with no vocational qualification, 46.6% dual training, 9.3% technical school, 18.5% degree: it includes pupils and students, so it was not used for adults 25-64; the Zensus 2022 Bildungsstand tables are in the script-driven Zensus database), Education at a Glance (Germany, adults 25-64: about 13% below upper secondary, 53% upper or post-secondary non-tertiary (mostly the dual vocational system), 11% short-cycle tertiary (Meister, Techniker), 23% bachelor or above; recalled, to confirm); years of schooling 9, 13, 14, 16 are placeholders. return_per_year_bps: placeholder 7% (German Mincer-type estimates run about 6-9%; to source); applied as productivity (Mincer 1974). max_years: placeholder. 2026-10-16: students_per_teacher 12.7 (was the placeholder 15): pupils per full-time teaching unit (Vollzeiteinheit) in the general-education schools of Niedersachsen, 12.72 in 2025 (12.86 in 2024): 883,783 pupils over 69,500 units (72,952 teachers by head count gives 12.1) (Niedersaechsisches Kultusministerium, 'Die niedersaechsischen allgemeinbildenden Schulen', Statistikbroschuere 2025, https://www.mk.niedersachsen.de/download/232075/Statistikbroschuere_abS_2025.pdf, Tables 6.3 and 6.4, opened 2026-10-16). It includes private schools and leaves out vocational schools. teacher_wage_per_pay_period (EUR 5,200 a month, A12/A13): the Besoldungstabelle was not reached; still a placeholder.
sources.elections: Niedersaechsisches Kommunalverfassungsgesetz (NKomVG): councils are elected every five years by proportional representation with three votes that may be piled on one candidate or spread across lists (kumulieren, panaschieren); the full-time mayor is elected directly, needing an absolute majority or winning a run-off (Stichwahl); both are approximated by 'preferential' (see gaps). Last general local election 13 September 2026; turnout 64.6% (preliminary result as reported by press and the Boell Foundation's Kommunalwiki, https://kommunalwiki.boell.de/index.php/Kommunalwahlen_in_Niedersachsen_2026; 57% in 2021; the Landeswahlleiterin's tables not opened, to confirm). stand_bps and news_readers_bps: placeholders (2%; 40% reading the local paper each week).
sources.nature: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2). cell_m: a cell is a 25 m lot. landscape.shares_bps: placeholder shaped by Niedersachsen's land use (about 60% agriculture and about 25% forest of the state's 47,710 km2; Landesamt fuer Statistik Niedersachsen, Flaechenerhebung; recalled, to confirm) for a lowland small town: 22% woodland, 3% scrub, 20% grassland, 50% farmland, 5% wetland. margin_cells, block_cells, woodland_patches, the covers' succession, the pollution figures, survey_hours_per_ha, survey_staff are placeholders as in the Australian profile (nothing region-specific; spin_up_years likewise).
sources.nature.species: Placeholders for growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection. red squirrel (Sciurus vulgaris): pre-breeding density 0.39-0.58 a hectare in heterogeneous habitat and 0.28 in a conifer plantation, home ranges 2-10 ha with an average of about 7 (summaries found in a web search of the red-squirrel literature, including studies in the Insubria and Durham repositories; the papers were not opened, to confirm), 0.4 a hectare of woodland used; strictly protected under the Bundesartenschutzverordnung (to confirm). great crested newt (Triturus cristatus): listed under the EU Habitats Directive annexes II and IV and 'gefaehrdet' (category 3) on Niedersachsen's red list of amphibians (NLWKN; found in a web search, 2013 list; to confirm); an average of 230 spawning migrants a year counted at one monitored site in 2012-2018 (NLWKN amphibian protection report; not opened, to confirm); the densities per hectare, home range, dispersal (up to 500 m) and tolerance of pollution are placeholders; it needs both ponds and land habitat close by. chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs), a common conspicuous control: 3.3 breeding pairs per 10 ha in one Austrian forest study (found in a web search; not opened, to confirm), so 0.33 pairs, 0.66 birds a hectare; other covers and the territory of 1.5 ha are placeholders.
sources.households: LSN, Zensus 2022: Landesamt fuer Statistik Niedersachsen (LSN), press release no. 074 of 19 August 2025, 'Zensus 2022: 78% der Singlehaushalte zahlten weniger als 500 Euro Nettokaltmiete', https://www.statistik.niedersachsen.de/presse/zensus-2022-78-der-singlehaushalte-zahlten-weniger-als-500-euro-nettokaltmiete-244136.html - of 3.8 million private households 41.2% one-person, 27% couples without children, 22% couples with children, 7.4% single parents (5.9 points of them mothers: 79.7% of single-parent households), 3% multi-person households that are no family. couple_bps is the remainder after the others are fixed (the published 27% is rounded). group_bps: the 3%, as 'multi-person households without a family core'. Opened sources: LSN press release 074/2025 (household shares and mothers' share of single parents) and Destatis, Statistischer Bericht Geburten 2024, table 12612-01 (Niedersachsen: 33,658 boys of 65,646 live births in 2024, so child_male_bps 5127). sources.support.payments: [The pension:] The statutory pension (gesetzliche Rente) is earnings-related, not flat. The structure takes one flat amount, so the Eckrente (a 'standard pension': 45 earnings points) is used: 45 x the current pension value of EUR 42.52 from 1 July 2026 (up 4.24% from EUR 40.79), set by the Rentenwertbestimmungsverordnung 2026 (Bundesrat Drucksache 243/26 of 30 April 2026, https://dserver.bundestag.de/brd/2026/0243-26.pdf, opened) = EUR 1,913.40 a month, gross, paid monthly. It is more than most pensioners get (a typical new pension is lower), and health and care contributions are deducted. Not means-tested. every_days 30 because German pensions are monthly. [The payment to those out of work:] The Regelsatz (Regelbedarfsstufe 1) of Buergergeld, EUR 563 a month for a single adult in 2026, unchanged from 2025 (Bundesregierung/BMAS, reported by finanz.de and the Buergerbeauftragte; to confirm against the Regelbedarfsstufen-Fortschreibungsverordnung; the 2026 reform to a 'Grundsicherung' is not reflected). Housing and heating costs are paid on top as actual costs (not modelled: the town's landlord is not paid by the state), and the first 12 months of unemployment are paid under insurance (Arbeitslosengeld I, 60% of previous net pay, 67% with children) which the structure cannot express. from_age 18 (adults; the under-25 rule that young people stay with parents is left out). Paid every 30 days. Means test left out. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track D of docs/design/profile-depth.md): support is now a list of payments, each a rule in three parts: who qualifies, how much, for how long (docs/behaviour/boundary.md); the law is published and the payments office reads it. The payments for those out of work end the year before the profile's retirement age (to_age): the rule the generator applied to every profile until now, written into the payment, where it can be changed. The pension is paid from the statutory pension insurance. EXPRESSED NOW, from this note: the first twelve months of unemployment are paid under insurance, 60% of previous net pay (67% with a child), for 360 days (twelve payments of 30 days), to those with contributions on the unemployment insurance's record; after it, or without a record, the flat Regelsatz as before. Previous pay is the mean of the monthly pay employers reported for the person; net is that less what the tax law's charges withhold from it. The note gives no figure for how long someone must have been insured (in the law, twelve months in the last thirty: docs/design/profile-depth.md section 4, to confirm), so any contribution on the record qualifies: the fields are `who.record.months` and `within_months`. Nobody has a record on the first day of a run, so those out of work at the start are paid the Regelsatz. Still left out: the means test and housing costs of the Regelsatz, the pension's earnings link.

sources.labour_force_participation_bps: Placeholder: the share of working-age adults (18 to the retirement age) in the labour force, about 80% (recalled: Germany's participation of 15-64 year olds is about 80%, Destatis / Eurostat; to confirm). Those outside it do not look for work.
sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Germany, national, annual 2025, from the EU Labour Force Survey: ages 25 to 54, 88.369%; 55 to 59, 85.112%; 60 to 64, 69.624%; 65 and over, 10.36%. How it is used: the first band is the reference; someone in the labour force stops work at the start of a later band with the chance these shares give, and those still in at the last band never stop. The survey's last band is open (65 and over), so nobody is drawn to stop after 65, and those who work on are older on average than they are in fact: to split when the shares at 65 to 69, 70 to 74 and 75 and over are opened. The profile's own participation figure (labour_force_participation_bps) still says how many are in the labour force at the reference ages; this curve says only how that share falls with age.

sources.public_finance.income_tax: Income tax tariff 2026, Einkommensteuergesetz para 32a (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__32a.html, opened): taxable income to EUR 12,348 untaxed (Grundfreibetrag); EUR 12,349-17,799: (914.51 y + 1,400) y; EUR 17,800-69,878: (173.10 z + 2,397) z + 1,034.87; EUR 69,879-277,825: 0.42 x - 11,135.63; above: 0.45 x - 19,470.38 (y and z are the income above the zone's start, in units of EUR 10,000). The marginal rate therefore rises linearly from 14% to 23.97% in the first zone and from 23.97% to 42% in the second. The structure takes marginal-rate steps, so the curve is approximated by 19% (about the mean of 14-24%) from EUR 12,349, then 29%, 34%, 39% as the 24-42% ramp passes EUR 17,800, 32,000 and 45,000 (the step values are my approximation), and 42% and 45% as written. levy: the employee's share of social insurance contributions in 2026, 21.15% = pension 9.3% + health 7.3% (the general rate is 14.6%, halved) + 1.45% (half of the average additional contribution of 2.9%; Federal Ministry of Health, opened) + care 1.8% + unemployment 1.3% (the pension, care and unemployment rates are recalled, not opened, to confirm), from the Minijob limit of EUR 603 a month, EUR 7,236 a year (Bundesregierung page above, opened). Contribution ceilings (pension EUR 101,400, health EUR 69,750 in 2026; recalled, to confirm) and the solidarity surcharge are left out; see gaps. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). The income tax keeps the author's steps approximating the continuous tariff (a schedule can now say a rate that rises in a straight line through a band, `rising_to_bps`, which is the tariff's two zones exactly: left for the author). UN-FOLDED: the levy of 21.15% that stood for the employee's social insurance is now its four contributions as this note gives them, each paid to its own body: pension 9.3% up to the ceiling of EUR 101,400; health 8.75% (7.3% and the 1.45% additional contribution) up to EUR 69,750; care 1.8%; unemployment 1.3%; each from the Minijob limit, as before. The note gives no ceiling for care or unemployment insurance (in fact they share the health and pension ceilings: to confirm), so none is set: the field is `base.up_to`. The employers' report of the unemployment contribution names each worker and their pay: the record the insurance payment is reckoned from. Not expressed: the solidarity surcharge (it would be a charge on the tax, `base.on`; the note gives no figure), the employer's share.
sources.public_finance.funds: The named funds and bodies of the higher government that this place's charges on pay are paid to, each kept as an account of the outside world's of its own (the general government's account takes the rest). Sets the town's opening rate. Waste and water are charged separately as fees (services, utilities); the trade tax and the income-tax share are not modelled. Note the 2025 Grundsteuer reform (new valuations) is in force from 2025 (to confirm).
sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Grundsteuergesetz para 28: property tax is due in four equal instalments on 15 February, 15 May, 15 August and 15 November (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/grstg_1973/__28.html, opened).
sources.public_finance.rates_due_days: Placeholder: an instalment falls due 30 days after its notice (in Germany the dates are fixed in the statute, see rates_instalments).
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Abgabenordnung para 240(1): a late-payment surcharge (Saeumniszuschlag) of 1% for each month or part of a month of delay (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__240.html, opened), so 12% a year.
sources.public_finance.rates_exempt_kinds: Land used for public service, schools, and hospitals and charitable purposes is not subject to property tax (Grundsteuergesetz paras 3-4; to confirm): here, the clinic's, the school's, the police station's and the utilities'.
sources.public_finance.median_house_price: Median asking price of a one- or two-family house in Niedersachsen, EUR 339,000 (EUR 2,158 a square metre), empirica for LBS NordWest, 2025, as reported by leinetal24.de, https://www.leinetal24.de/niedersachsen/niedersachsen-an-gefragten-standorten-auf-hohem-niveau-so-teuer-sind-immobilien-aktuell-in-94095224.html (asking prices, not sale prices; the original not opened, to confirm). The land value of a lot is derived from it: this less what the builder charges.
sources.services.waste_per_person_per_day_g: Placeholder: about 460 kg of household waste per person a year (Destatis, Abfallbilanz; recalled, to confirm), a day's worth in grams.
sources.services.landfill_levy_per_tonne: (Left out since 2026-10-09: the landfill charge, which stood here as nought for a rule the place does not have. The note is its author's, as written.) 0: Germany levies no landfill tax (landfilling untreated waste has been banned since 2005; waste incineration pays the national CO2 price under the Brennstoffemissionshandelsgesetz from 2024; both are not modelled; to confirm). See gaps.
sources.services.council_staff_per_1000: Placeholder carried over from the Australian profile (about 6 per 1,000, all of them the works crew); Germany's municipal staff is much larger (kindergartens, hospitals, social services), Destatis, Personal des oeffentlichen Dienstes (to source).
sources.services.collect_seconds_per_10kg: Placeholder: a one-driver side-loader lifts up to 6 bins a minute (Bucher Municipal, Sport side loader); with driving between houses, about 1,000 bins a day is taken as a round, and a household's week of waste as about 24 kg: about 12 seconds of work per 10 kg.
sources.services.asset_life_years: Placeholder: a park or civic building wears out in 15 years without upkeep (after VAGO, Maintaining Local Roads: spray seals last 10-15 years).
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: Placeholder: a crew member's half a day a week keeps a park or the hall up (mowing, bins, repairs).
sources.services.complain_bps: Placeholder: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. Who reports and who doesn't varies (the service-request literature, e.g. Stowers 2022, State and Local Government Review); a rate is to be sourced.
sources.public_service.wage_per_pay_period: [SECONDARY] TVöD-VKA / TVöD-V pay group 6 (Verwaltungsfachangestellte-level clerical), step 3, valid 1 May 2026 to 31 March 2027: EUR 3,580.46 a month (a pay-scale aggregator's table, oeffentlichen-dienst.de, and a city's published 2026 table; not opened on the TVöD text itself), times 12 over 26 = EUR 1,652.52. Group 6 was chosen as a typical clerk; a caseworker (group 8) would be about a fifth higher. Gross, without special payments. 2026-10-16: confirmed: TVoeD-V pay group 6, step 3, EUR 3,580.46 a month from 1 May 2026 to 31 March 2027, after 2.8% (oeffentlichen-dienst.de/tvoed-v.html, a pay-scale aggregator, opened; the VKA table is assumed to carry the same figures). Banking staff: about 554,000 employees nationally at the end of 2024, 6.5 to 7.6 per 1,000 (dasinvestment.com, opened; secondary), which supports the national base, not the 4.0 local share.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.administra: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated at about 3 FTE per 1,000 residents for a town's own offices (finance, taxes, planning/building, registry, clerk, youth office liaison), excluding works crew, kindergartens, schools. Derived from a search snippet that efficient municipalities in NRW run about 5-7 core staff per 1,000 residents in all (small ones), of which general administration is roughly half; Destatis Fachserie 14 Reihe 6 tables by task area were not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.courts: [PLACEHOLDER] About 0.2 FTE per 1,000. Niedersachsen's justice service has about 11,200 staff (Ministry of Justice / Haufe report, 2019-20), for about 8 million residents (1.4 per 1,000) including prosecutors and prisons; the civil Amtsgericht/Landgericht share is assumed to be about 15% (assumption, to confirm). 2026-10-16 (not applied): all Niedersachsen courts and the prosecution had about 11,500 staff in December 2025 (ordinary courts 8,379, prosecution 2,156, specialised courts about 1,300; head count), 1.2 per 1,000 for the courts without prosecution, with criminal and family work and bailiffs in it; the civil and labour part is not separable (Justiz in Niedersachsen flyer, opened). 0.2 stays.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.oversight: [PLACEHOLDER] About 0.015 FTE per 1,000: a state consumer-advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale Niedersachsen, assumed about 100 staff) plus the Bürgerbeauftragte's small office (assumed about 10 to 20) for about 8 million residents. Both headcounts recalled, not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.elections: [PLACEHOLDER] About 0.005 FTE per 1,000: the Landeswahlleiter's permanent office is a few dozen staff for the state; elections are run by municipal staff on the day. Estimate, not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.land_regis: [PLACEHOLDER] About 0.07 FTE per 1,000: Grundbuchämter at the Amtsgerichte, assumed about 500-600 staff in Niedersachsen for about 8 million residents. Not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.press: [PLACEHOLDER] About 0.15 FTE per 1,000: Germany has about 12,000 editors at daily newspapers for about 83 million people (about 0.14 per 1,000; BDZV figure, recalled, to confirm); a local paper's editorial desk is taken at that density.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.banking: [PLACEHOLDER] About 4 FTE per 1,000 residents served: German credit-institution employment is about 570,000 for 83 million (about 6.9 per 1,000, Bundesbank/BdB, recalled), of which a local Sparkasse/Volksbank (branch, lending, payments) is taken as a bit over half. To confirm.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.utilities: [PLACEHOLDER] About 1.5 FTE per 1,000: a municipal Stadtwerke's water and energy-retail operations, estimated from about 0.9 per 1,000 for water supply and wastewater and about 0.6 for retail/customer service. No source opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.union: [PLACEHOLDER] About 0.12 FTE per 1,000: the DGB unions' full-time officers number roughly 10,000 nationally (recalled, to confirm) for 83 million residents.
sources.public_service.licences.payment_system: [PLACEHOLDER] EUR 15 a year per resident served for a core-banking and payments platform: a rough order of magnitude from a bank's IT cost per customer (shared-service IT providers such as Finanz Informatik or Atruvia charge their banks per account); no price list found.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.property_m: [PLACEHOLDER] Carried over unchanged to every profile: property managers (people who run let homes for their owners) at about one to every 100 to 150 let homes is an industry rule of thumb (to confirm, not opened); a town here has about 380 homes for 1,000 people, so about 3 per 1,000 residents. A manager looks after the letting offices of several landlords.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.audit: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated from the real audit office headcount over the population it serves: Niedersaechsischer Landesrechnungshof (about 170 staff from memory) plus the Kommunalpruefungsanstalt (about 100 from memory) and the municipal Rechnungspruefungsamt, over about 8m residents: about 0.04. Headcounts from memory, not opened (to confirm). Basis: Grundgesetz art 114 (Bundesrechnungshof), Niedersaechsische Verfassung art 70, and the Niedersaechsisches Kommunalverfassungsgesetz on the municipal audit.
sources.audit.office: [MIXED] Niedersaechsischer Landesrechnungshof and the Kommunalpruefungsanstalt (Lower Saxony), the Bundesrechnungshof for federal money, and the kommunale Pruefungsaemter, under Grundgesetz art 114 and the Niedersaechsisches Kommunalverfassungsgesetz. Named from memory, not opened (to confirm). The neutral name is the platform's.
sources.audit.answer_within_days: [PLACEHOLDER] The Rechnungshof's right to ask for papers has no day count that was opened; 28 days is an estimate (to confirm).
sources.audit.report_within_days: [PLACEHOLDER] The municipal annual accounts are audited after the year's end and the audit report is due within about half a year; 180 days is an estimate from memory (NKomVG; not opened; to confirm).
sources.audit.bodies: [PLACEHOLDER] Periods: decisions every 90 days (a quarter) and accounts every 180 days (an interim, half-yearly examination between the annual audits, so that a year of the run holds two), in line with annual financial audit under INTOSAI ISSAI 1000/2000 and an audit sample of 15% of the period, at least 6 and at most 25 decisions, a size chosen for a town of 1,000 to 100,000 under ISA 530 audit sampling (not opened; to confirm). The support office is the outside world's, so only its decisions are checked; the town finance office is checked on accounts. The chosen sample share is the platform's, not the law's.
sources.public_service.appointed_by: [PLACEHOLDER] Who fills the post of a public body when none of its own staff is left: the town's council, which seconds one of its own staff to it, as a local government assigns officers to bodies it runs. Real places mostly give these appointments to a state body, a minister or a board, none of which the town models, so the council stands in for them (to confirm per place). The paper, which the town keeps on a grant as it keeps the courts, is counted with them (2026-10-25; WM-7). Bodies run on their own account (the bank, the union, landlords, shops) are not covered: their owners or members would appoint, and no owner's or member's office exists to do it.
sources.unions.membership_bps: 'other' (the overall rate): 14.1% of employees were union members in Germany in 2024 (OECD, Trade union density, series TUD, percentage of employees, https://sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TUD_CBC@DF_TUD,1.0/DEU...; 15.9% in 2016, falling; opened 2026-10-08). By industry (manufacturing 19%, construction 15%, retail 9%, public administration 24%): placeholders (IG Metall, IG BAU, ver.di strength; to source from the WSI Mitgliederbefragung or Destatis). Keyed by the industries employers' postings name.
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Placeholder: 90 days; German unions' rules usually allow leaving only with written notice to the end of a quarter (ver.di Satzung; to confirm), which the structure can only express as a notice period.
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once (a registered association, Verein: BGB para 39 lets a member leave at any time, with a statute-set notice of up to two years; to confirm).
sources.unions.dues_per_month: Placeholder: EUR 30 a month, about 1% of a gross monthly pay of EUR 3,000, the dues rule of ver.di and IG Metall (their constitutions; recalled, to confirm).
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more. Settlements are measured against the Destatis' Tarifindex or the WSI Tarifarchiv's collective wage increases (average annualised wage increases in new agreements), a calibration target.
sources.households.age_bands_bps: LSN, population by age group as a share of Niedersachsen's population on 31 December 2024 (0-4: 4.5%, 5-9: 4.9%, 10-14: 4.6%, 15-19: 4.8%, 20-24: 5.2%, 25-29: 5.8%, 30-34: 6.1%, 35-39: 6.4%, 40-44: 6.1%, 45-49: 5.7%, 50-54: 6.4%, 55-59: 8.2%, 60-64: 7.9%, 65-69: 6.5%, 70-74: 5.4%, 75 and over: 11.3%), table A100011G, read from a regional profile of the Elbe-Weser region that quotes the state (IHK Stade, 'Regionalstruktur: Demografische Merkmale des Elbe-Weser-Raums', data retrieved 2025-07-17, https://www.ihk.de/blueprint/servlet/resource/blob/3390782/480bf1a16d99f22db0c57cbca47ed845/bevoelkerung-data.pdf); shares sum to 99.8% and are scaled to 100%. The split of 75 and over into 75-79 (4.7%), 80-84 (3.4%) and 85 and over (3.2%) is a placeholder. Mean age 45.1 (Niedersachsen-Monitor 2025). Adults living alone, as couples without children at home, or in groups are drawn from this less the parents the family shares imply (docs/behaviour/households.md).
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.groups.kinds: The kinds of group in a German town, mostly registered associations (Vereine; about 600,000 in Germany, ZiviZ-Survey; recalled, to confirm): sport (the sports club, the largest by members), religious, arts and culture, hobby and interest. How often each meets and for how long are placeholders. Whether people come is theirs; participation is a target, not a rate given to anyone.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: Placeholder carried over: the share of adults who belong to a group at the start and go to its gatherings, 40%. German volunteering and association membership (Freiwilligensurvey 2019: 39.7% volunteer; Deutscher Olympischer Sportbund: about 28 million memberships in sports clubs; to confirm) is the nearest target.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words: content, for belief to attach to (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 5). The congregation's stands for the Christian denominations together (one congregation per town is a simplification).
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: Placeholder 50%: roughly half of people in Niedersachsen belong to a Christian church (the Evangelical Church of Hanover alone had about 2.4 million members and the Catholic Church in the state about 1.2 million; Germany-wide, Catholic 24.8% and Protestant 22.7% in Zensus 2022; recalled, to confirm). At the start the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly and others up to this share hold it less; after that it strengthens, spreads and fades.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people (Germany has far more associations per head; to source).
sources.households.child_max_age: The Zensus and Mikrozensus count children of any age living with their parents; family statistics count unmarried children living at home without their own child or partner as children. Children at home are drawn up to 24 (a simplification: older children at home are left out).
sources.automation: (PB-6) The outside world's offers of systems to businesses (docs/behaviour/automation.md). Prices are those of vendors in US dollars, converted at an approximate 2026 rate of 0.92 EUR to the dollar (to confirm; the rate is not the place's own and is not read by any code), into the currency's smallest unit; they are the outside world's, held at today's level unless a yearly change is given, like world prices. self-service-point: a bank of self-checkout or self-ordering units: set-up about US$15,000 (a unit's list price runs US$15,000 to 25,000 installed in retail trade reports; to confirm), a yearly licence and support about 16% of it (support contracts run 10 to 20% of the hardware; to confirm), three years' licence, US$3,000 to leave. It does a share of the task 'serve' (scope: placeholder, 30%, in the range of the share of a retail worker's tasks that Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin and Rock 2023 find exposed to current systems; to confirm) in as long as a person takes (placeholder). production-cell: an automated line or cell: set-up about US$90,000 for a cell (the installed cost of an industrial robot system is a few times the robot's price of about US$50,000: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics; to confirm), a yearly licence and maintenance about 10% of it, five years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it does 35% of the task 'make' (placeholder) in 70% of a person's time (placeholder). oversight_hours_per_month and error_bps are placeholders (what looking after one costs the buyer's own staff; how often it gets a unit wrong, refunded at the unit's price). case-handling-system: a system that writes an office's routine papers (a rates notice, a permit decision) and records them: set-up about US$40,000 and a yearly licence of 30% of it (a public-sector case-management system's price; placeholder, to source), three years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it writes them in 15% of a clerk's time (placeholder) and can do 60% of them (placeholder, in the range Eloundou et al. 2023 give for clerical work; to confirm). Mistakes: 2% of papers (placeholder; automated administration's error rates are a documented risk: Michigan's Auditor General found most fraud determinations of its unemployment system wrong, 2016 (to confirm)).
sources.automation.price_fall_bps_per_year: 0: the outside world's prices for systems are held at today's level (the default); a scenario (worlds/scenarios/falling-system-prices.yaml) gives a yearly fall, with its basis.
sources.automation.firms: (PB-6) How a business weighs a system (docs/behaviour/automation.md). payback_months: the months over which the costs of changing (set-up, exit) must be repaid, 24 for a small business and 36 for a large one (ten staff or more): placeholders, in the range firms report requiring for equipment of two to three years (Graham and Harvey 2001, 'The theory and practice of corporate finance', Journal of Financial Economics; to confirm). hurdle_bps: the margin by which the saving must beat the cost, 20% (placeholder, a margin of safety for a manager's own estimate being unsure). reference_bps: each business already using it that the vendor names eases the hurdle by 2 points, never below nothing (Mansfield 1961, 'Technical change and the rate of imitation', Econometrica; Griliches 1957; Rogers 2003: uptake follows how many have taken it up; the size is a placeholder). on_cost_bps: what staff cost beyond their wage, 0: the world models no employer's charges beyond the wage and redundancy pay. most: the most systems of one kind it takes at once (placeholder).
